bib.title: Ethical Challenges in Data-Driven Dialogue Systems

read.skipped: References skimmed only; supplemental material (GitHub) not available

question: What ethical and safety problems arise in data-driven dialogue systems (bias, adversarial inputs, privacy, safety, RL, reproducibility), and how large are they in small demonstrative experiments?
hypothesis: Data-driven dialogue models absorb and can expose bias, offensive content and private data from their training data, and are fragile to input perturbations.
contributions: Survey of ethical issues in dialogue systems
New demonstrative experiments on dataset bias, word-embedding debiasing, adversarial inputs and privacy leakage

method.summary: Small demonstrative experiments: classifier-based bias/hate/offence scoring of four dialogue corpora and of HRED/VHRED samples; LSTM LMs with Word2Vec vs debiased embeddings; misspelling and paraphrase perturbation of a VHRED retrieval model; a seq2seq secret-key recovery test on Ubuntu.
method.task: ethics and safety analysis of end-to-end dialogue systems

results.claim: Secret key-value pairs in under 0.1% of training data are recovered by a seq2seq model with near-perfect accuracy when the key is supplied.
results.setup: seq2seq on 10k Ubuntu pairs plus 10 keypairs (5-word key/value), UUID and English-vocab types; subsampled-word keypairs harder
results.quote: the model learns to elicit the private in- formation simply by inputting the triggering information se- quence (key) with nearly 100% accuracy
results.note: quote has hyphenation line breaks in source; sensitive data < 0.1% of data

results.claim: Debiased Word2Vec shifts LM gendered follow-up distributions only about 1-2.5% toward even.
results.setup: LSTM LMs on 1B-word benchmark, 50 male- and 50 female-stereotyped professions, 1000 samples each
results.quote: only see- ing a ∼1 −2.5% overall change toward even distribu- tions

results.claim: Male-stereotype triggers yield 75.45% male follow-ups with Word2Vec and 74.37% with debiased vectors.
results.table: Table 2, row Male Stereotypes, column Word2vec Male

results.claim: Reddit Politics has 4.50% offensive-language and 2.38% hate-speech utterances; Twitter 3.63% and 0.63%.
results.table: Table 1, row Reddit Politics, column Offensive Language

results.claim: Models trained on Twitter reproduce offensive language: HRED stochastic sampling 4.06% offensive vs 3.63% in the Twitter data.
results.setup: HRED stochastic sampling on Twitter validation contexts
results.table: Table 1, row HRED Model Stochastic Sampling (Twitter), column Offensive Language

results.claim: One-character edits to inputs cut response similarity to about 0.75 cosine (Politics) or 0.67 (Movies), while input similarity stays about 0.94.
results.setup: VHRED retrieval model, 20 base sentences, 1000 character edits each, Reddit Politics
results.table: Table 3, row Politics Character Edit, column Generated Response Similarity

results.claim: Evangelist trigger: follow-ups about 83% male, 71% with debiased vectors.
results.quote: sees a followup dis- tribution which is about 83% male

limits: Small demonstrative experiments with no seeds, significance tests, or stated hyperparameters in the main text (deferred to supplemental GitHub).
Bias detectors are imperfect; they misclassified 'killing a process' as hate speech.
Adversarial notion for generative dialogue is acknowledged as an open problem; only 20 base sentences used.
Privacy test is on a small seq2seq with 10 injected keypairs; generalisation is asserted ('We expect'), not shown.
Pre-LLM (2017) models; no conditional safety guarantees offered.
practices: Release code, pre-trained models and training details to allow reproducibility (Reproducibility).
Use data augmentation with generated adversarial examples during training (Adversarial Examples).
Consider automated anonymization and differential privacy for conversational models (Privacy).
Aim for conditional safety guarantees via a model trained to predict unsafe behaviour, bounding probability of unsafe response (Safety).
Constrain RL exploration and bound rewards on unsafe behaviour (RL).

terms.definition: one that an agent takes, which does not cause any offensive or harmful effects to human interlocutors
unintended or harmful behaviour resulting from poor design
